lots.key_photo_findings: One photo (450 x 600 px). Design, lettering ('jantzen' over 'SUNSHINE SUPERMAN') and colours match dealer copy CL197-101, which I compared side by side; the small black 'L' on the right-hand figure's lower leg is in the same place on both, so it is printed artwork, not a mark or damage. No printer's credit, date code or designer signature legible at this size. Aspect ratio about 1.47, consistent with the dealer's 99.8 x 66.7 cm. Hung by four bulldog clips; top edge wavy and the top corners curl; no tears, fold lines or tape visible at photo size (edge-enhanced check). Back, the areas under the clips and the paper surface are not shown.
lots.condition: Unframed, unbacked, curling at the top corners with a wavy top edge; colours look bright; no tears, folds or tape visible at photo size. Back, clip areas, pinholes and any trimming not shown. Whether it is a period print or a later reproduction cannot be told from the photo.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you check whether the poster is an original period print or a later reproduction (screenprinted ink layers rather than an offset dot pattern under a magnifier, aged paper, any printer's or designer's credit in the margins), confirm its size (the dealer copy is 99.8 x 66.7 cm), and report any tears, pinholes, folds, tape or repairs, front and back, especially under the clip areas?

lots.what_it_is: Freestanding oval cheval (dressing) mirror, H160 x W66 cm: bevelled oval plate in a narrow oval frame pivoting between plain square uprights, on a trestle base with a plain stretcher and two shaped, scroll-cut foot pieces. Strong fiddleback figure in golden to reddish-brown timber, consistent with Tasmanian blackwood, but the catalogue does not name the timber. Simple Federation or Arts and Crafts form, probably early to mid 20th century, small-maker or home-workshop construction.

lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD = $60 hammer (Gowans lot 711, 31/07/2026, the closest design) / 1.22 = $49.18, round down to $45 hammer (about $54.90 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $80 hammer in a Tasmanian room (middle of the $60 to $100 close results; the fiddleback figure may help a little), less about 15% seller commission ($12) and $0 outbound postage (160 cm tall, local pickup sale) = $68; $68 / 2.44 = $27.87, round down to $25. Pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay, inbound freight $0, but it needs a vehicle. The flip margin is very thin, so this is really a keep-only lot.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification and three close Tasmanian SOLD results within 24 months (records opened, photos compared), but the timber is not confirmed as blackwood, there is no maker's mark, and the back of the mirror and the glass condition are not shown.
lots.dropped_entries: Chairish 12855894 (US$1,100 ask, https://www.chairish.com/product/12855894/wooden-cheval-mirror) and Chairish 37166212 (US$360 ask, https://www.chairish.com/product/37166212/vintage-cheval-mirror-in-wood-1960s): both pages opened and live at those prices, but they are a 1960s Virginia Mirror Co. cheval and a narrow French beech mirror offered at US retail, shipping to North America only: different items in a different market, so no evidence for this lot. Gowans lot 1616 (412524, $115, 29/05/2026): sold together with a shield-back chair, so a bundle price. Gowans lot 1472 (420519, $105, 03/07/2026): oval mirror standing on a single-drawer base, a different item. Gowans lot 1306 (420353, $2, 03/07/2026): damaged, not comparable. All three Gowans records were opened and match the researcher's figures.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Enlarged crops show strong ripple (fiddleback) figure on the foot pieces, stretcher and oval frame, with plainer straight grain on the uprights; the uprights are through-tenoned into the shaped foot pieces; simple knob pivot fittings; bevel visible on the oval plate. No maker's label, stamp or mark seen. A small pale spot on the stretcher beside the right-hand upright (possibly a filled hole or knock). Reflections make the glass hard to judge; possible light spotting near the left edge. Back of the frame and plate, the underside and the far feet are not shown.
lots.condition: Appears sound and complete as far as seen; light wear to the foot edges; possible light silvering spots near the edge of the plate; back of the mirror, pivots and underside not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the timber Tasmanian blackwood? Is the mirror plate original, with any silvering loss or chips to the bevel, do the pivots hold the mirror at an angle, and is there any maker's label or inscription on the back?

lots.guide_summary: Same item or close: 14 sold, 0 unsold, 4 asking. Same item inside 24 months, all US auctions: US$60, US$85 and US$125 (A$86 to A$180). Same item outside the window: A$20 at Lawsons Sydney (03/10/2024, the only Australian sale found, generic title), US$90 twice and US$35 with wear (2024, US). Close (Butterfly Gold trios, or sets with round bowls or extra pieces): US$50 to US$150 (A$72 to A$216). Asking: four live US Poshmark listings, US$199 to US$350 (A$286 to A$503), not prices paid. Category only: Australian rooms paid A$35 to A$140 for other retro Pyrex (A$25 and A$120 passed in), and Gowans mixed lots with one Butterfly Gold casserole made $55 and $80. USD at 1.437 (ECB, 16/10/2026).
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD inside 24 months in similar condition = US$60 (Matthew Bullock lot 12, 22/11/2025) x 1.437 = A$86.22; / 1.22 = $70.67, round down to $70 hammer ($85.40 all-in). Flip: likely resale about A$86 (that same lowest in-window sale; the higher US results are out of reach from Tasmania because posting four glass bowls overseas costs too much), less about 15% selling fees ($12.93) and $0 postage (local pickup sale) = $73.29; / 2.44 = $30.04, round down to $30. Caution: every in-window sale is American. The only Australian sale of this exact set made A$20 (Lawsons, 03/10/2024, 16 days outside the window) and Australian rooms paid A$35 to A$70 for other retro Pyrex nests and trios, so treat $70 as a ceiling and expect it may sell well below. Pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay; inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Pattern and set make-up are read clearly in the photos and there are three same-item SOLD results inside 24 months (pages opened; prices from Invaluable's own index because the pages hide them behind a login), but all are US sales, the only Australian same-item sale was A$20, and the bases (marks, chips, wear) are not photographed.

lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Butterfly Gold print (butterflies and flowers) read on all four bowls; Cinderella shape with twin handle-spouts; alternating white and gold in the right 441 to 444 sizes, nesting fully. Gloss looks good and no chips are visible on rims or spouts at photo size; the gold print on the smallest white bowl looks slightly thin. A few dark specks on the outside of the 444 (dust or wear, unclear). Lot stickers on the 444 rim. The bases, where the PYREX mark, size number and any wear would show, are not photographed.
lots.condition: Complete set of four, glossy, no chips or cracks visible at photo size; slight print thinning on the 441; base marks, base wear and scratches unchecked.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please check the bases: are all four marked PYREX with 441, 442, 443 and 444, and are there any chips (especially on the spouts and base rims), cracks, heavy utensil scratches or dishwasher-dulled print?
